A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ExPLoRA research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial layout changes and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original ExPLoRA results on satellite and WILDS datasets, together with ablations, representation analyses and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments including compute-allocation comparisons and VisDA-2017 evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains selective block unfreezing, trainable normalization layers and LoRA updates to frozen blocks' Q/V matrices. The DinoV2, MAE and multispectral adaptations remain the same. New optimization notation and use as an initialization for UDA do not establish a changed ExPLoRA procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds VisDA-2017 synthetic-to-real classification using ExPLoRA initializations for TVT and SSRT, extending evaluation to a conventional UDA setting. Existing satellite and WILDS coverage is retained. Office-Home and FireRisk are discussed but not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1/4 add GFM and GDA; Table 1 adds ScaleMAE with LoRA; Tables 1/16 add Mona and Adapter+ comparisons. Table 4 removes the ImageNet-supervised ResNet152 comparator. New VisDA comparisons include CDTrans, PMTrans and alternative TVT/SSRT initializations. Earlier MAE PEFT rows are retained in Table 16.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces total-compute comparisons using 50k–200k pre-training checkpoints and direct fine-tuning controls with different trainable-parameter budgets. Appendix B.7 adds pre-training on both VisDA domains followed by TVT/SSRT evaluation with ViT-B and classwise/mean accuracy. Existing training schedules and preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new compute-allocation study tests whether extended pre-training is preferable to spending resources on direct fine-tuning. Table 3 adds an MLP-only LoRA ablation, and Figure 4 newly displays eigenvalue variance. Earlier convergence, decoder-rank, backbone-size, attention-map and patch-probing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added eigenvalue-variance plot concerns feature representations, not uncertainty across experimental runs; the existing attention-score truncation procedure is unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial baseline, compute-curve and VisDA results, including TVT/ExPLoRA at 88.2% and SSRT/ExPLoRA at 90.9%. Table 3 adds the 48.55% MLP-only result. Table 1 updates ExPLoRA's listed fMoW-RGB accuracy from 79.15% to 79.28%, while Table 4 removes the 54.46% ResNet result. Most retained benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 5–6 add explicit constrained-optimization formulations and parameter-space definitions for pre-training and downstream adaptation. Appendix A.2 adds formal UDA assumptions, including target/source label-set containment. These are limited formal additions; the existing weight decompositions remain and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main method and contribution claims remain. The introduction now explicitly claims advantages of up to 16-fold fewer trainable parameters and eightfold less compute, and strengthens the WILDS description from generalization to outperforming baselines and prior work. The abstract's linear-probing headline changes from 7.5% to 8%.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning limited final-accuracy benefits beyond 50k pre-training iterations, eigenvalue variance as evidence of local/global information encoding, and ExPLoRA's complementary role as a UDA initialization. Existing qualifications about SpaceNet and reduced iWildcam linear-probing performance remain.

D1.justification: New experiments document checkpoint-specific GPU-hour costs, fine-tuning control configurations and the VisDA initialization recipe. Section 5 explicitly explains merging updates into the original ViT. The earlier training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, code-access statement and dataset-license information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises domain-adaptation positioning and expands adapter-related coverage. New Appendix A contrasts ExPLoRA with GFM/GDA and traditional UDA using architecture preservation, objective flexibility, source-data access and label restrictions. Several classical adaptation citations and the ReLoRA discussion are removed.

P1.justification: v3 refines domain/task notation, consolidates method and storage explanations, promotes the analysis subsection to Section 7 and reorganizes appendix material. Much of the existing introduction, experimental discussion and limitations retains its wording and narrative sequence.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged vertically and moved to the first page; Figure 2 gains explicit block-set annotations. Tables are restructured, MAE comparisons receive an appendix continuation, and new comparison tables, a variance plot and a compute plot are added.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central efficiency argument through direct GFM/GDA comparisons and a total-compute study separating extended pre-training from additional fine-tuning, both absent in v2. The UDA experiments and Appendix A also improve applicability evidence and research positioning. New reporting inconsistencies need correction: the stated TVT improvement conflicts with Table 17, and claimed parameter matching conflicts with Figure 7's labels. These localized problems limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains in relevant evidence.
